subject.title: [Feature]: Granular session visibility — split tools.sessions.visibility into per-capability knobs

question: Should OpenClaw add a structured per-capability `tools.sessions.visibility` model, or should send/history/list separation be solved through a different session authorization shape?
rationale: This changes a public config surface and the transcript/privacy boundary between cross-agent messaging and cross-agent read/list/status access, and it overlaps open per-agent, allowlist, sandbox, and A2A-send proposals.

options.title: Approve per-capability visibility
options.body: Adopt a validated object or equivalent canonical shape that can allow cross-agent send without granting cross-agent history/list/status, with compatibility shorthands and isolation tests.

options.title: Fold into broader scoping
options.body: Make this issue subordinate to a broader per-agent or session-key allowlist design if maintainers prefer agent/session axes over capability-specific controls.

options.title: Keep all-or-nothing visibility
options.body: Reject the granular split and document `visibility="all"` plus A2A allow rules as the intentional operator opt-in for cross-agent coordination.

recommendation.title: Approve per-capability visibility
recommendation.body: Adopt a validated object or equivalent canonical shape that can allow cross-agent send without granting cross-agent history/list/status, with compatibility shorthands and isolation tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The history pass shows the strongest connection to the session access/resolution helpers and the current shared visibility boundary.
